item.title: Spectroscopy of the SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system under the influence of the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
item.description: arXiv:2610.33611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the ground state spectrum of a dynamical scalar-fermion-gauge system with an SU(2) gauge group, a scalar doublet, and two degenerate generations of vectorial fermions under the influence of the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect. To this end, we employ lattice methods using the HiRep code. We study the dependence of the system on the (bare) fermion mass and find that the spectrum remains unaffected, up to trivial fermion mass effects. The results are in line with a weakly coupled theory exhibiting the Fr\"ohlich-Morchio-Strocchi mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Axel Maas, Sofie Martins, Georg Wieland

item.title: Two-Particle Correlation Function in a Finite Volume
item.description: arXiv:2610.33681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the two-particle correlation function in a finite volume. First, defining an unphysical complex-energy sheet of the correlation function and identifying unstable states as poles on the sheet, we demonstrate that the expansion of the correlation function, which includes poles of unstable states, holds up to exponentially decreasing corrections with the volume size. Based on this result, we show that the finite-volume correction to the complex energy of the unstable state also decreases exponentially with the volume size, namely that finite-volume corrections are relatively small for the unstable states. Then, we show that the imaginary-time correlation function in a finite volume approaches that of the infinite volume as $\tau/L^2 \rightarrow 0$ while it is dominated by the lowest energy mode as $\tau/L^2 \rightarrow \infty$, where $\tau$ is the imaginary time, $L$ is the volume size. In drawing these conclusions, we first present a qualitative, general discussion and then demonstrate quantitative results using simple nonrelativistic models with a contact interaction (EFT) and a separable potential.
item.dc:creator: Wren Yamada, Osamu Morimatsu, Toru Sato, Koichi Yazaki

item.title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory define a family of probability distributions that forms a statistical manifold, and its Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. In the large-$N$ limit of the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ is taken to zero with the mass gap $\Lambda$ fixed, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $\sigma$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and the Fisher metric of the full $P(\sigma)$. In the former, the lengths of the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term shrink, relative to the mass-term direction, to order $a\Lambda\log(1/(a\Lambda))$ or smaller, and when several modes are combined, only the two directions $(\Lambda,m)$ of the continuum theory remain. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink at the same rate as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in correlations at distances of the order of the lattice spacing. An exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator: as $a\to0$ its length goes to zero in both metrics, and it becomes indistinguishable from a change of the coupling $1/g^2$ (a lattice version of Kutasov's result). The curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(a\Lambda))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point is infinitely far in Fisher distance from any point at finite $a$.
item.dc:creator: Akio Tomiya

item.title: Pion vector form factor from LapH-smeared currents in lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.34397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore a method to extract pion vector form factor from three-point functions using currents constructed from LapH-smeared quark fields. LapH employs the low eigenmodes of the Laplacian Heaviside operator on the lattice to smear out the quark fields in spatial directions. The LapH-smeared quark propagator retains all symmetry properties of the original one and can be re-used to construct correlation functions at a reduced cost, with equal treatment of connected and disconnected diagrams. The calculations are performed on a two-flavor dynamical nHYP-smeared ensemble on the $24^3\times 48$ lattice at a spacing of 0.12 fm and pion mass of 315 MeV. We show that an extrapolation in the number of low eigenmodes in the LapH subspace can reproduce the same form factor computed from the conventional SST method with point source, sink, and current. The study opens up the possibility of applying LapH-smeared currents to extract hadron form factors and polarizabilities including disconnected diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Frank X. Lee, Andrei Alexandru

item.title: Large-$N$ $\pi^+\pi^+$ scattering from twisted Eguchi--Kawai reduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.35176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the first computation of the $\pi^+\pi^+$ scattering length in large-$N$ QCD in the 't Hooft limit, $N_{\scriptscriptstyle{\rm f}}/N\to 0$, using the twisted Eguchi--Kawai formulation of the lattice theory. We employ values of $N$ up to 1156 and consider several quark masses and lattice spacings to achieve controlled large-$N$, continuum, and chiral limits. The chiral behavior of the scattering length is compared with next-to-leading-order Chiral Perturbation Theory predictions. Our result for the low-energy coupling describing the sub-leading quark-mass dependence is consistent with existing S-matrix bootstrap bounds. Combining TEK results with previous lattice QCD data obtained using standard methods for $3\le N\le 6$, we are also able to extract sub-leading $\mathcal{O}(1/N)$ corrections to the large-$N$ scattering length.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Bonanno, Margarita Garc\'ia P\'erez, Antonio Gonz\'alez-Arroyo, Ken-Ichi Ishikawa, Masanori Okawa, Fernando Romero-L\'opez

item.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.35524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power $p$ close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that at finite disorder strength $W$ of moderate strength, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, this power $p_1$ vanishes and the spectrum features a very accurate power behavior with $p<0$ on an interval around $E = 1$ spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E = \infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. We show that $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E)=-1$ for all energies accessible by our data. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, to model the IR sector of the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be viewed as descending from the randomness strength $W$ rather than the lattice size $L$.
item.dc:creator: Ji\v{r}\'i Adam, Andrei Alexandru, Navdeep Singh Dhindsa, Ivan Horv\'ath, Frank X. Lee, Nilmani Mathur

item.title: Toward Compute-Bound Lattice-QCD Software
item.description: arXiv:2610.35526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-right-hand-side multigrid inverters for lattice QCD are much less memory constrained than single-right-hand-side Krylov solvers, so the upper bound on efficiency of modern solvers is much higher than what was historically possible. This work presents a reanalysis of roofline estimates to reflect this new reality. It also describes the qc library, which implements multi-right-hand-side multigrid at an efficiency that can exceed 50% of the processor roofline.
item.dc:creator: Anthony V. Grebe

item.title: Annealed sampling of diffusion models in lattice field theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.35792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning methods have recently gained increasing interest as possible means of solving critical slowing down in lattice field theory, with particular emphasis on sampling methods using field transformations such as normalizing flows, annealing/out-of-equilibrium methods, and diffusion models. Annealing methods provide appealing polynomial scaling and exactness guarantees, while diffusion models use a simple and efficient score-matching training procedure. This work explores a method combining these benefits, first training an energy-based diffusion model using score matching, then sampling using either stochastic normalizing flows (SNFs) or flow-transformed replica exchange (T-REX). The choice of sampling method can be made after training the diffusion model; the theoretical properties of SNFs and T-REX and their relative trade-offs are discussed. Numerical results are presented for scalar field theory and the O(3) non-linear sigma model, using a class of local-footprint energy models with efficient gradient and divergence calculations. Sampling from the trained models follows predicted exactness and scaling properties, and significantly improves over sampling methods without a learned component.
item.dc:creator: Gurtej Kanwar, Octavio Vega

item.title: A Low Scale for Quark-Lepton Unification
item.description: arXiv:2610.33152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The measured fermion masses may be pointing to the scale of quark-lepton unification. Studying the renormalization-group evolution of the Standard Model Yukawa couplings, we find that $y_\tau=y_b$ and $y_\mu=3y_s$ occur at nearly the same scale, around $10^6$ GeV, while the first generation reaches the Georgi-Jarlskog relation $y_e\simeq y_d/3$ at order $10^8$ GeV and can arise from the same Clebsch structure through a simple hierarchical flavor texture. This pattern naturally suggests low-scale Pati-Salam symmetry. We show that flavor mixing and finite threshold corrections preserve this picture. If the electron mass has an independent origin, the two heavier-generation relations can be realized in theories with a unification scale as low as $(5$-$7)\times10^5$ GeV. We identify two simple theories that accommodate all three relations and in which the measured masses fix the flavor structure. The first unifies all three generations at $4.6^{+1.2}_{-0.9}\times10^6$ GeV; the second, with symmetric Yukawa matrices, at $1.5^{+0.7}_{-0.5}\times10^7$ GeV, and predicts $|V_{cb}|=0.042\pm0.002$. Their shared light-family texture fixes the relevant vector-leptoquark couplings, making $\mu\to e$ conversion in nuclei a direct test of unification: upcoming searches will probe part of the region selected by the two theories, and proposed facilities could cover it completely.
item.dc:creator: Lawrence J. Hall, Claudio Andrea Manzari, Clara Murgui

item.title: Fixed Points of the Yang-Mills Gradient Flow in the Vortex Sector
item.description: arXiv:2610.33874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Yang-Mills gradient flow of center vortices in SU(2) gauge theory. For axially symmetric vortices the flow reduces exactly to a linear diffusion equation for the radial profile: a Gaussian core keeps its shape while its width grows as $\sqrt{R^2+4t}$, the flux is exactly conserved, and the thin vortex is the unique bounded fixed point, though not an attractor. Off-diagonal perturbations are governed by a pair of radial Schr\"odinger operators, and a variational computation shows that, frozen at any instant, the Abelian core has a tachyonic mode for every winding $n\geq 1$. Since the core spreads while the mode grows, we pass to self-similar variables, where the unstable modes are known in closed form, with growth exponents $\mu_{n,m}=n-1+m$. Multiply wound vortices are therefore unstable, while the fundamental vortex is exactly marginal and stays Abelian. A scaling argument rules out any static vortex in the transverse plane, and the instability acquires a simple geometric meaning that shortens the path traced in SU(2) by the holonomy of a growing loop, lowering the winding by two. The flow thus drives every vortex toward the Abelian core of winding $n \bmod 2$, with non-Abelian structure appearing only as the transient through which multiply wound cores unwind.
item.dc:creator: A. M. Silva

item.title: Nucleon polarizabilities revisited: insights from the Bernab\'eu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach sum rule
item.description: arXiv:2610.34276v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a complete dispersive evaluation of the Bernab\'eu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach (BEFT) sum rule for the nucleon dipole polarizability difference $\alpha_{E1}-\beta_{M1}$. The analysis is based on hyperbolic dispersion relations, which separate the $s$- and $t$-channel contributions without double counting and are particularly suited to backward real Compton scattering. This framework makes it possible to precisely determine the polarizability difference from independent dispersive input rather than from fits to low-energy Compton scattering data. The $s$-channel part is updated with modern single-pion photoproduction multipoles and model estimates of non-$\pi N$ inelastic channels. For the $t$-channel, we use contemporary dispersive input for $\gamma\gamma\to\pi\pi/K\bar K_{I_t=0}$ together with Roy-Steiner equation solutions for $\pi\pi/K\bar K_{I_t=0}\to N\bar N$, and we extend the calculation to the isovector $\pi\eta/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ channel associated with the $a_0(980)$. The resulting treatment resolves the long-standing puzzle of earlier BEFT evaluations driven by the scalar-isoscalar two-pion channel and gives a controlled estimate of the subleading isovector contribution. Combining the resulting BEFT values with the Baldin sum rule, we obtain, in units of $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, \[ \alpha_{E1}^p=11.17(52),\quad \beta_{M1}^p=2.84(52),\quad \alpha_{E1}^n=12.18(59),\quad \beta_{M1}^n=3.03(59). \] For the proton, these values provide a benchmark with a precision comparable to state-of-the-art dispersive and chiral effective field theory extractions. For the neutron, whose polarizabilities are much less directly constrained experimentally, the result provides an independent dispersive benchmark with an uncertainty comparable to that of the proton.
item.dc:creator: Xiong-Hui Cao, Ling-Yun Dai, Feng-Kun Guo

item.title: Nucleon tomography from a calibrated diquark spectator model
item.description: arXiv:2610.34602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) provide a unified description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse spatial structure of the nucleon. We calculate the twist-2 vector GPDs $H^{q}$ and $E^{q}$ in a spectator model containing both scalar and axial-vector diquark configurations. A central new result is the explicit analytic expression for the axial-vector-diquark contribution to the helicity-flip GPD $E^{q}$. To regulate the transverse-momentum integrations while retaining a physically sensible dependence on the momentum transfer, we introduce a momentum-transfer-dependent quasi-hard cutoff. The model parameters are determined through two complementary calibrations: one using proton observables only and another simultaneously including proton and neutron observables. Electromagnetic moments and radii, together with selected constraints on gravitational form factors, determine the quark and diquark masses, the relative scalar and axial-vector contributions, and the transverse-momentum scale. The two calibrations yield compatible parameter ranges, while the inclusion of neutron observables reduces the parameter uncertainties and more strongly constrains the flavor structure. From the resulting zero-skewness GPDs $H^{u,d}(x,0,t)$ and $E^{u,d}(x,0,t)$, we calculate the valence-quark PDFs and the impact-parameter distributions of unpolarized up and down quarks in both unpolarized and transversely polarized nucleons. The transverse distributions exhibit the expected localization of large-$x$ quarks near the transverse center of momentum and a flavor-dependent distortion when the nucleon is transversely polarized. Our results provide a unified phenomenological description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse-position structure of valence quarks in the nucleon.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Terlecki, Shohini Bhattacharya, Krzysztof Cichy

item.title: Two-Pion Exchange Paradigm in Hadron-Hadron Interactions from Lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.34655v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study hadron-hadron interactions in (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD near the physical pion mass ($m_\pi \simeq 146\mathrm{MeV}$) using the HAL QCD method, with particular emphasis on two-pion exchange (TPE). The nucleon--flavor-singlet hadron potentials such as $\phi$-$N$, $J/\psi$-$N$, and $\eta_c$-$N$ are found to be attractive at all distances. Moreover, in the long-range region where one-pion exchange is forbidden, we observe lattice signatures consistent with TPE dominance. These results demonstrate that the HAL QCD method can extract universal long-distance phenomena, such as TPE, directly from nonperturbative QCD dynamics.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Subatomic Particles and Cosmology, 5 (2026) 100341
item.dc:creator: Tetsuo Hatsuda

item.title: Interaction dependence of the critical correlation length amplitude ratio in anisotropic scalar lattice $\phi^4$ theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.35081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate critical correlations in the weakly anisotropic two-dimensional scalar lattice $\phi^4$ theory and demonstrate that a previously reported independence of the correlation length amplitude ratio from the local interaction strength does not hold. Monte Carlo simulations instead reveal a pronounced dependence of this ratio on the interaction strength. As the coupling is increased, the amplitude ratio interpolates between the continuum and Ising limits, highlighting a nontrivial interplay between lattice effects and local interactions. These findings call for a revised theoretical description of anisotropy effects at finite coupling in this prototypical lattice field theory.
item.dc:creator: Leonie M\"uller, Stefan Wessel

item.title: QCD on the 16-cell honeycomb
item.description: arXiv:2512.10604v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate QCD discretized on the four dimensional 16-cell honeycomb. The advantage is a higher degree of rotational symmetry as compared to a traditional cubic lattice leading to much smaller cut-off effects. We demonstrate in quenched QCD, through both gluonic and fermionic observables, that the scaling properties are indeed superior to the cubic lattice and much larger lattice spacings are sufficient for controlled continuum extrapolations. Chiral and topological properties also show remarkable improvement.
item.dc:creator: Sandor D. Katz, Daniel Nogradi

item.title: Third moments of nucleon unpolarized, polarized, and transversity parton distribution functions from physical-point lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2605.02808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using forward matrix elements of local leading-twist operators, we present a determination of the isovector third Mellin moments $\left< x^2 \right>$ of nucleon unpolarized, polarized, and transversity parton distribution functions. Two lattice QCD ensembles at the physical pion mass are used, which were generated using a tree-level Symanzik-improved gauge action and 2+1 flavor tree-level improved Wilson Clover fermions coupling via 2-level HEX-smearing. Leveraging a wide set of operators, two extraction methods for the matrix elements, and the automatic inclusion of model uncertainties via bootstrapped model averages, we extract values of the third Mellin moments. This is the first direct calculation of these observables performed at the physical pion mass.
item.dc:creator: Emilio Taggi, Michael Engelhardt, Jeremy R. Green, Stefan Krieg, Stefan Meinel, John W. Negele, Andrew Pochinsky, Marcel Rodekamp, Sergey Syritsyn

item.title: A different kind of continuum limit for the three-dimensional U(1) gauge theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.27976v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In three-dimensional compact U(1) lattice gauge theory color confinement can be understood analytically through the dynamics of magnetic monopoles. However, its continuum limit is pathological, since the ratio of the glueball masses to the square root of the string tension vanishes as the continuum limit is approached. We investigate a simple extension of the Wilson action in which the total number of lattice monopoles is coupled to an additional parameter $\mu$. By tuning $\beta$ and $\mu$ simultaneously, we identify a line of constant physics along which the ratio of the lightest glueball mass to the square root of the string tension remains constant. We further show that the same scaling is satisfied, within numerical uncertainties, by the other low-lying glueball masses considered in this work. Along this trajectory, the string tension in lattice units decreases with increasing $\beta$, thus suggesting that the modified lattice action may provide a regularization of three-dimensional compact U(1) gauge theory with a physically well-behaved continuum limit.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Athenodorou, Claudio Bonati, Ivan Soler Calero

item.title: Towards a consistent perturbation theory at finite temperature
item.description: arXiv:2606.14863v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The standard approach to perturbation theory for finite-temperature quantum field theories has several issues, including the appearance of ill-defined on-shell contributions in the real-time formulation, and infrared divergences in massless theories. Earlier studies indicate that these issues all stem from the inconsistent thermal generalisation of the Gell-Mann-Low relation, which forms the foundation of perturbation theory in vacuum. This inconsistency arises from the use of free scattering states in the relation, which are known not to exist in interacting thermal theories. In this work, we propose a generalisation of the Gell-Mann-Low relation for scalar theories based on non-perturbative spectral insights, namely that finite-temperature scattering states can be described by damped but stable particle-like excitations, so-called thermoparticles. The perturbative expansion of this generalised relation gives rise to contributions with exactly the same topology as the standard finite-temperature approach, except that now the propagators appearing in this expansion are not those of a free field but of thermoparticles, which depend on the dynamics of the theory. We demonstrate that thermoparticle perturbation theory resolves the known problems of the standard approach. Furthermore, by comparing imaginary-time calculations at two-loop level with numerical lattice simulations of two-point correlation functions in massive $\phi^{4}$ theory, we explicitly show that this framework gives rise to precise predictions, as in the vacuum case, in stark contrast to the standard approach.
item.dc:creator: Passant Ali, Peter Lowdon, Owe Philipsen

item.title: Probing the $B^{0}$ meson in a hot medium with finite chemical potential
item.description: arXiv:2609.08299v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We employ QCD two-point sum rules to determine the $B^{0}$ meson mass and decay constant as functions of temperature $T$ and chemical potential $\mu$, using the perturbative spectral density and nonperturbative contributions up to mass dimension five. Numerical analysis indicates that, in the limits $T \to 0$ and $\mu \to 0$, the mass and decay constant of the $B^{0}$ meson are in good agreement with the available experimental data. Furthermore, at fixed chemical potentials, the $B^{0}$ meson mass and decay constant initially increase with temperature, reach their maxima, and then decrease to zero, with the increase being more pronounced for the decay constant than for the mass. The temperatures at which both quantities vanish decrease as the chemical potential increases. At fixed temperatures, both quantities initially increase slightly with chemical potential before decreasing and eventually vanishing, with the mass exhibiting a much weaker decrease in vacuum. The vanishing points of both quantities shift toward lower chemical potentials as the temperature increases, following a trend similar to that observed in the QCD phase diagram. The results obtained in this study are expected to contribute to the interpretation of data from ongoing heavy-ion collision experiments and to the generation of data for future planned experiments focusing on $B$ mesons, quark-gluon plasma signatures, and dense matter environments.
item.dc:creator: A. T\"urkan, G. Bozk{\i}r, K. Azizi

item.title: Precision Sum Rule for Nucleon Isovector Polarizabilities and the Proton-Neutron Mass Difference
item.description: arXiv:2609.15154v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The precision of the electromagnetic proton-neutron mass difference $\delta m_\mathrm{QED}$ extracted from the Cottingham formula hinges on a subtraction function whose low-energy normalization $\bar S(0)$ is fixed by the isovector combination of the proton and neutron polarizabilities, $(\alpha_{E1}-\beta_{M1})^{p-n}$. We derive a dispersive sum rule for this combination in terms of $s$-channel photoabsorption cross sections and the product of $t$-channel $\gamma\gamma\to\pi\eta/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ and $\pi\eta/K\bar K_{I_t=1}\to N\bar N$ amplitudes, without invoking Reggeon dominance. Combining empirical pion-photoproduction multipoles with coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omn\`es representations of the scalar-isovector $\pi\eta/K\bar K$ amplitudes, we obtain $(\alpha_{E1}-\beta_{M1})^{p-n}=-0.82(33)\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, fixing its sign and reducing the uncertainty by one order of magnitude compared with the previously known value. This result yields $\bar S(0)=-0.56(28)\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$, leading to $\delta m_\mathrm{QED}=0.75^{+0.02}_{-0.04}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, substantially more precise than previous Cottingham determinations. The negative $\bar S(0)$ also provides a low-energy test of Reggeon dominance in the subtraction function.
item.dc:creator: Xiong-Hui Cao, Ling-Yun Dai, Feng-Kun Guo
